reasoning: I agree with the Market Analyst's risk-off call (SPY 5.54% under its 200-day, 20-day vol 26.55%, all eleven sectors down over 5 days); the regime filter allows only BND, GLD, IEF and TLT, with BND and IEF wash-sale blocked. Held-book review (L7), from the stop blocks: no stop_alerts; the closest are SAM (3.26% above $201), INCY (4.2% above $110) and IDXX (5.66% above $640). WMT's stored clause is met: XLP's 21-day return is +0.52%, below +3%. I approve the full sale (P1). The Skeptic argues the clause fired on a market-wide drop while Staples still leads, and wants it rewritten as a relative test. On 11-20 the PM removed 'while SPY holds' so that this clause could trip in a falling market. Rewriting it on the day it trips would make stored invalidations meaningless. The sale also cuts the largest bucket (Staples, L3), which WMT and KR now share through the Grubhub sounding-out. All other clauses are untripped. TLT: 5d +2.61% and IEF +1.79% while SPY -8.56%, so the duration clause is not met. KR: the cyber matter is unconfirmed, and the Grubhub contact is not a bid or an 8-K. SAM: the CEO handover took effect today with no guidance change, and SAM is still on the menu. INCY: no guidance cut or failed pivotal trial, and Mizuho raised its target. DPZ: the insider sale is not an 8-K event; DPZ is still on the menu with CFO above NI. IDXX, MSCI, VRSN and CARG: no filings. CARG (Communication) and VRSN (Technology) sit in sectors the Market Analyst now avoids, but neither thesis rests on a sector role, so L8 needs no restatement. I approve the IDXX half trim (P2), which L8 said was owed: IDXX is the highest-beta single stock in a high-vol tape. The Skeptic's hold case (Health Care is dropped, not avoided; the $640 stop already locks in a gain) is reasonable but only caps the downside on half. I resize the TLT add (P3) from $20 to $10. I accept the Skeptic's data point: market.json is as of 11-20, so the hedge has one more session of evidence, not another week, and TLT's 21-day return is only +0.06% against SPY's -9.71%. A $20 add would take TLT above the $40 the PM rejected on 11-20. $10 follows the Market Analyst's explicit duration preference (L4: not a diversification-only token) and keeps TLT on its own stop (L9). Cash after these trades is about half the account. That cash is idled by the regime filter, not by choice, and no invalidated position is kept because of it. When the filter reopens, deployment goes first to Staples-light and Utilities names with their own stops, sized against buckets. L6: TLT's stop is restated today from the $80.75 fill. Stale text (DPZ's dollar-loss figure and 10-20 lines, VRSN's add rationale, CARG's dated rank, IDXX's owed-trim line) is cleaned up through thesis_updates. L2: dates are from the News Analyst's filings check (IDXX next 2027-02-01; WMT next is a 2027-02-18 file estimate).

thesis_updates.thesis: A small defensive Treasury sleeve while the regime filter allows only BND, GLD, IEF and TLT. The Market Analyst says Treasuries are the better defensive choice and prefers intermediate and long duration. TLT is used because IEF and BND are wash-sale blocked, not because he prefers it over them. It is the most volatile Treasury option, and the hedge rests on a short run of evidence (TLT's 21-day return was flat while SPY fell), so it was bought at $25 on 11-20 and added to by only $10 on 11-23. It adds long-duration rate risk that the equity stress test does not show, and the 12-09 FOMC falls inside its 20-session test. TLT tracks 20+ year Treasuries and is judged not substantially identical to the blocked IEF. ETF, no earnings events. No other bond ETF is held.
